main_text.p: testium veritatis, crebra lectione teritur martyrologium magnum, parvum, utrumq; plenum viris veritatem professis, quorum memoria Jesuitarum impudentiam satis confundere potest. His auctoribus per lectis demū eant, & cū Mülhufino dicant: Ostendant, obsecro, tandem quis illam (veram religionem) professus sit prater ecclesiam Romanam clientes, qui mille jam & quingentos annos (priusquam cucullum exeussisset Lutherus, & seditionibus replesset Gallias Calvinus) in orbe terrarum universo, vocati sunt Christiani, eoq; nomine a Judæis, a paganis, ab hereticis, extremas injurias & persequutiones per pessi? Non illi, inquiunt, sed alii soli Deo cogniti, hominibus ignoti illam professi sunt. Frigidum hoc simul & imprudens responsum. Fateor sanè non frigidū, sed frigidissimum, non imprudens, sed & imprudentissimum esse responsum: at non ab orthodoxis datum, sed à levifido ac temerario Jesuita excogitatum, illisq; calumniosé imputatum. Sed refutationis compendium quo istorum hominum convicium dignabimur, hic à Menandro docemur:
Ὁ λοιδορῶν γὰρ, ἂν ὁ λοιδορούμενος
Μὴ σκευσωρήσῃ, λοιδορεῖ' ὁ λοιδορῶν, h.e.

page.notes: Greek lines transcribed from a small, slightly blurred print; the accents and the final letters of lines 3 and 4 are uncertain and should be checked against the scan (the word "σκευσωρήσῃ" in line 4 in particular is a best reading). "frigidū" at the line end is probably frigidum with a printed mark; "Convi•" may be a catchword followed by a printer's dot. The "h.e." after the fourth Greek line is printed as shown. Ink bleed and stains on the right margin; no words lost.
